title: Interleaving String
summary: Determine whether s3 can be formed using every character of s1 and s2 exactly once, preserving the order within each source string.
statement: Determine whether s3 can be formed using every character of s1 and s2 exactly once, preserving the order within each source string. At each step take the next character from either source; repeated characters may require considering both choices.
constraints: s1 and s2 have 0–100 lowercase letters; s3 has 0–200 lowercase letters.
Use every character of s1 and s2 exactly once while preserving each source's internal order. Characters may be taken from either source at each step.
hints: If both sources can supply the next character, a greedy choice can be wrong.
Let a state say whether prefixes s1[:i] and s2[:j] can form s3[:i+j].
A state is reachable from the previous s1 prefix or previous s2 prefix when the added character matches; update one row left-to-right.
Reject unequal total length immediately, and initialize the empty-prefix state to True.
editorial: A prefix state may consume its final character from either source. Combine both valid predecessor states with OR, preserving alternatives when characters repeat. With one row, the old current-column value represents the preceding s1 prefix and the already-updated left value represents the preceding s2 prefix. The length check and empty-prefix initialization cover empty inputs. The oracle independently enumerates positions assigned to s1 and checks the complementary positions against s2.

tests.explanation: The chunks aa + dbbc + bc + a + c alternate sources and preserve both source orders.
The character counts fit, but no assignment of positions preserves both source orders, so return False.
